title: DOW-UAP-D61, Mission Report, Arabian Gulf, August 2020
what_is_it: A declassified U.S. military Mission Report (MISREP) documenting an ISR surveillance flight over the Arabian Gulf region on August 27, 2020, during which a formation of unknown flying objects was observed.
core_summary: A U.S. Air Force ISR aircraft from the 482nd Attack Squadron took off from Al Udeid Air Base (OKAS) on August 26, 2020 and conducted a 21-hour reconnaissance mission supporting NAVCENT operations in the Arabian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman. At 1527Z on August 27, the aircrew observed a formation of unknown flying objects traveling northeast to northwest along the coast for approximately two minutes before losing tracking due to light cloud coverage. The crew was unable to reacquire positive identification of the formation.
interpretation_warnings: Heavy redaction throughout: aircraft type, callsign, exact grid coordinates, personnel names, operation name, and ATO details are all redacted under various exemptions (1.4a, 1.4g, 3.5c, b(3), b(6))
The aircraft type is fully redacted, though sensor suite (ANDAS4, AH/GMESH) and mission profile suggest an unmanned ISR platform
The UAP observation lasted only approximately 2 minutes before being lost in cloud cover — very brief window for characterization
The method of observation was sensor-based, not visual, but the specific sensor used for the UAP observation is not stated
The description 'formation of unknown flying objects' is the reporter's subjective characterization at the time; no sensor data, imagery, or technical analysis is included in this report
The weather section explicitly notes clouds prevented continuous tracking, meaning the observation data is incomplete
This is a single-source report from one aircrew/platform with no corroborating observations mentioned
The document was declassified 19 years ahead of its original 2045 declassification date, as part of a broader USCENTCOM UAP disclosure effort
The report notes the intelligence gap was not filled, suggesting the UAP formation was not identified or resolved

public_headline: U.S. Military Crew Tracked Unknown Flying Objects Over Arabian Gulf in 2020
public_tldr: A declassified U.S. Air Force mission report documents a 21-hour surveillance flight over the Arabian Gulf on August 27, 2020, during which the aircrew's sensors detected a formation of unknown flying objects traveling along the coast. The crew tracked the formation for roughly two minutes before losing it in cloud cover and could not reacquire it.
public_narrative:
On August 27, 2020, a U.S. Air Force aircraft assigned to the 482nd Attack Squadron was conducting an aerial reconnaissance mission over the Arabian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and the Gulf of Oman in support of Naval Forces Central Command (NAVCENT). The aircraft had launched from Al Udeid Air Base the previous evening and would fly for just over 21 hours total.

At 1527Z (approximately 3:27 PM UTC), the aircrew's onboard sensors picked up a formation of unknown flying objects moving northeast to northwest along the coastline. The crew tracked the formation for about two minutes before light cloud coverage obscured it. They were unable to regain positive identification afterward. The report notes the method of observation was sensor-based, not visual, though the specific sensor used is not stated.

The mission report, designated Misrep 4685903, was originally classified with a scheduled declassification date of March 1, 2045. It was released early on January 22, 2026, as part of a broader U.S. Central Command disclosure effort — 19 years ahead of schedule. The report is heavily redacted: the aircraft type, crew names, exact coordinates, operation name, and other operational details are all blacked out.

Beyond the unknown objects, the mission documented routine regional surveillance activity, including a professional-toned radio hail from Iranian Air Defense, a small vessel docked at Greater Tunb naval port, and a possible IL-76 transport aircraft at Abu Musa Island airfield. The report explicitly states that the intelligence gap the mission aimed to fill was not resolved.
public_caveats: This is a single-source report from one aircrew on one platform. No corroborating observations from other aircraft, ships, or ground stations are mentioned in the document.
The UAP observation lasted only about two minutes before cloud cover ended tracking — a very short window that limits what could be determined about the objects.
The report is heavily redacted. The aircraft type, crew identities, exact location coordinates, and operational details are all withheld, making independent verification difficult.
The phrase 'formation of unknown flying objects' is the reporting crew's characterization at the time. No sensor imagery, technical analysis, or follow-up assessment is included in this document.
The report confirms the intelligence gap was not filled, meaning the objects were never identified or explained within this mission's scope.
